public_source_audit.outcome: The publisher pseudocode loops over N crossover offspring, while indexed author-shared full-text prose describes the fittest offspring's candidate position. The figures show a Chebyshev sequence in [-1,1] labeled C1=0.65 but do not expose the executable recurrence, sequence lifecycle, or Equation 12. The cited OLCGOA predecessor narrows the blend's lineage without defining OLCE semantics, and an earlier open Chebyshev-Mayfly paper also omits its recurrence and lifecycle. DOI/discovery records, public archives, institutional profiles, and repository and code searches expose no author implementation resolving the three stable questions or the source's cardinality conflict.

sources.finding: The version-of-record landing page confirms the article identity, authors, dates, affiliation, corresponding author, abstract, figures, and references. The accessible page is a subscription preview and links no supplementary code, data, or implementation archive.

The authoritative mating pseudocode creates N crossover offspring before chaotic exploitation. Together with Figure 3 it supplies an all-N executable path, but it does not reconcile the indexed full-text prose's fittest-offspring description. Mayfly follows the figure loop as a documented library choice, not as a resolved paper-wide cardinality claim.

The authoritative pseudocode loops from 1 through N, generates a Chebyshev chaotic-variable sequence Cx_it for the current iteration, mutates an offspring according to Cx_it, evaluates the mutant, and updates gbest. It conflicts with the indexed full-text prose's fittest-offspring wording, does not print the recurrence, seed, sequence advancement rules, or component formula, and uses loop variable i versus offspring subscript k inconsistently.

The authoritative plot labels the Chebyshev sequence C1=0.65 and shows values in [-1,1]. A plotted trajectory and probability curve do not uniquely identify the recurrence, its order or parameter, indexing convention, or component mutation equation.

The publicly indexed author-shared text describes Equation 12 as changing the candidate solution of the fittest offspring's position and defines its symbols as an offspring component, constriction factor, and motion bounds. The equation itself is not exposed as searchable text, and the fittest-offspring wording conflicts with Figure 3's loop through N.

The DOI record confirms the bibliographic identity, exposes version-of-record text-mining links, and confirms that the paper cites the OLCGOA predecessor DOI 10.1016/j.eswa.2020.113282. Its relation object is empty and it identifies no dataset, software deposit, supplement, or reference implementation.
The official Crossref text-mining PDF URL returned the subscription landing HTML with access marked No to an anonymous request, not a PDF containing Equation 12. No access control was bypassed.

OLCE's publisher-supplied Crossref references cite OLCGOA. Its author-shared full text gives the analogous candidate equation CS=(1-s)*Fbest+s*C'_i for the best grasshopper, but a different algorithm's equation cannot establish OLCE's Equation 12, offspring cardinality, replacement rule, or sequence lifecycle.

This open Chebyshev-Mayfly paper states that its map fluctuates in [-1,1] and replaces two uniform random variables with two chaotic numbers randomly selected from the chaos. It prints no Chebyshev recurrence, initialization, sequence-generation algorithm, or deterministic consumption lifecycle, and Crossref does not list it among OLCE's references.

The discovery record reports one closed version-of-record location, no open-access location, no repository full text, and no content URL. Author-identity suggestions from this secondary index were not treated as primary contact evidence.
Nanjing Tech University's current Xiaoping Su profile supplies a public contact address and research biography but links no OLCE-MA or MAOLC implementation, experiment archive, or raw runs.
An exact-DOI public repository search returned zero repositories. This records the search outcome and does not prove that private or unindexed code is absent.
An exact-title public repository search returned zero repositories.
An authenticated public-code search returned zero MATLAB files for MAOLC; searches for the DOI and Equation 12's Mayflyoffspring token exposed no external implementation.
The public archive index exposed captures of the publication's Figure 1 and Figure 4 images but no archived article PDF, full-text asset, source archive, or deterministic trace.

blocking_questions.question: What exact Chebyshev-map recurrence generated Cx, what does the printed C1=0.65 denote, and how was the initial state or seed selected?
blocking_questions.known_evidence: Figure 4 plots a sequence in [-1,1] and labels C1=0.65, while Figure 3 only says to use a Chebyshev map. The earlier open Chebyshev-Mayfly paper also supplies no recurrence or initialization and merely says that chaotic values are randomly selected from a sequence. None of these sources gives an executable equation, order or control parameter, seed policy, or indexing convention for OLCE.

exact_chaotic_exploitation_gate.rule: Mayfly may replace its documented Logistic-map compatibility extension with a paper-faithful OLCE-MA chaotic-exploitation stage only after all three questions have non-null answers backed by cited primary evidence, the full-text fittest-offspring prose is reconciled with Figure 3's all-N loop, and the resolved implementation passes recurrence-, sequence-, component-, lifecycle-, bounds-, evaluation-accounting-, and serial/parallel-conformance tests.

correspondence_draft.subject: Request for OLCE-MA/MAOLC Chebyshev mutation equation and reference implementation
correspondence_draft.body:
Dear Professor Su and co-authors,

I am implementing the chaotic-exploitation stage from your 2022 article, An enhanced Mayfly optimization algorithm based on orthogonal learning and chaotic exploitation strategy (doi:10.1007/s13042-022-01617-4). Figure 3 loops over N crossover offspring, while the indexed full-text prose describes the candidate solution of the fittest offspring's position; Figure 4 labels a Chebyshev sequence C1=0.65 in [-1,1]. I cannot recover three details needed for an executable, paper-faithful implementation: (1) the exact Chebyshev recurrence, all constants or order parameters, the meaning of C1=0.65, and the initial-state rule; (2) whether chaotic exploitation targets all N offspring or only the fittest and how Cx_it is reset, advanced, and indexed across generations, selected offspring, and D components, including how i, k, it, and D in the pseudocode relate; and (3) the complete offspring-component mutation equation referred to as Equation 12, including the constriction factor s, bound mapping or repair, replacement rule, best-state updates, and objective-evaluation accounting.

Could you please share the original MAOLC/OLCE-MA source or the complete equations and clarify those lifecycle rules and the prose/pseudocode cardinality difference? A small deterministic trace with the initial chaotic state, generated Cx values, one input offspring batch, the selected and mutated positions, and evaluation/best updates would also make an equation-level conformance test possible. Version identifiers or checksums would help keep the result auditable.

Thank you for your time.
